items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: Joe Dixon was in that band at the time.

ctx.x: This was '37. All in '37. So, I'm making four arrangements a week and copying them. For the band. Myself. I couldn't (inaudible). I was trying to make all of that money. I didn't want to give the money -- and, Jimmy Munday was also here writing for Benny Goodman at the time, and I -- I got a room right across the street from Jimmy Munday, and I was staying up on the 135th right off of Seventh Avenue, and Munday was staying across the street downstairs. He had like an English basement apartment.

And, so, we would go down and write together and talk and everything, and I would be doing my work, he would be doing his work. So, I took -- the first rehearsal we had in New York, I had my four arrangements and I took them down. So, Gus Arnheim says, "Just a minute, Budd, before you rehearse the band." Now, he said, "Gentlemen, I want you to know this now. Budd Johnson, as you know, is the musical director. He's the arranger for the band. And, if he tells me anybody can't play his music, then you better look…
